sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who sets the value
sections.html:
The people who send your bill and the people who value your property are different offices. The Bartow County Tax Commissioner mails and collects. The Board of Tax Assessors decides what your land and house are worth. Payments, mobile home accounts and tax sale overage claims all go to the commissioner's suite in the Frank Moore Administration and Judicial Building, 135 W. Cherokee Avenue, Suite 217A, Cartersville. The property tax line is (770) 387-5111, and the counter takes visitors Monday to Friday from eight until five, holidays aside.

Bartow has a sole commissioner form of government. A single elected commissioner approves the budget and fixes the millage in a public meeting held in that building. Cartersville is the county seat. Adairsville, Euharlee, Kingston and Taylorsville have their own charters, while Cassville, Rydal and Allatoona are unincorporated communities that still pay through the county office.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, duplicate bills, excess funds forms
  • Board of Tax Assessors: your value, returns and the notices that start your appeal clock
  • County Commissioner: sets the rates and the budget each summer

sections.h2: Bartow County for a home seller
sections.html:
Up in northwest Georgia, the Cartersville end of the county now acts like an Atlanta exurb along I-75. Population moved from 100,157 in 2010 to 108,901 in 2020, with an estimate of 120,800 for mid-2025. A large industrial base, a battery plant and data center development have lifted the tax digest, and that growth has let the millage keep falling.

Housing totals 50,010 units in 2025, and 72.8 percent of households own. The middle owned home is valued at $289,000, middle rent is $1,268 a month and middle household income is $82,243. Cartersville addresses fall under Cartersville City Schools, and most others go to the Bartow County School District, so verify the district before you tell a buyer which one applies.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Expect your real estate statement near September 15. Payment is due November 15. Mobile homes work differently and are due April 1.

The January 1 owner is the person billed. If you bought after that date, call the tax office and request a duplicate in your name, since the first statement went to the seller before you. Not receiving a bill does not change the deadline.

  • Online payment is a link on the Tax Commissioner page, which also points to qpublic for parcel lookups
  • Any debit or credit card payment, online, at the counter or by phone, picks up a 2.5 percent convenience charge
  • Make a mailed check payable to the Bartow County Tax Commissioner and send it to the Cherokee Avenue address

Georgia holds off interest for 60 days after the bill's postmark, though overdue balances may collect penalties on top. Ask the counter what your own account shows.

The 2026 rate is 7.11 mills inside city limits and 6.76 mills in the unincorporated county, down from 7.40 and 6.87 the year before. The commissioner chose the rollback rate, and rates have trended down since 2013.

Each mill is a dollar of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value, and the assessed figure is 40 percent of fair market value. Your bill also carries a school levy, so it reflects more than the county rate. For the combined millage on your parcel, ask the tax office.

Bartow County billing at a glance
Billing itemBartow County
Statements mailedAbout September 15
Real estate due dateNovember 15
Inside city limits (2026)7.11 mills, down from 7.40
Unincorporated areas (2026)6.76 mills, down from 6.87
Card payment surcharge2.5%
Mobile home due dateApril 1

When the bill arrives, check three things before you do anything else: the parcel and owner name, the district shown for schools, and the combined millage. A wrong name or district is easier to fix in September than at the closing table.

A bill that arrives after you have sold belongs in the buyer's hands, so forward it right away. Mobile home owners should note that the April 1 account is separate from any real estate bill on the same land, and each has to be settled on its own.

Apply before April 1. Only the house you actually live in counts. Rentals, multi-family buildings and commercial or industrial property do not qualify.

The standard exemption is $15,000 of value. Local leaders hope to raise it to $30,000 in a future year, so phone the office for the amount on your current bill. A move to another Bartow house means a new application for the new address, and whoever buys yours must file too, because your exemption stays behind.

To dispute the value, mail a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark no more than 45 days after the notice date. Every Georgia county uses that window, and it applies to fair market value disputes.

Ahead of any notice, an owner may file a return from January 1 to April 1 naming the value they think is right. Tax charged in error can be reclaimed within three years of paying it, and a winning appeal brings an automatic refund. Before you write, write down your reasoning and collect sale prices of nearby houses and dated photos of damage.

A tax debt stays with the property, so closing is when it should be cleared. Since the statement is addressed to the January 1 owner, a seller who held title that day normally gets it even when the deed transfers in October. Your closing agent can lay out how the year is divided and who mails the check.

If back taxes pile up and the county sells a parcel for more than the debt, the extra money is held for people with a claim, and the commissioner's page links an excess funds form. Selling before a levy usually costs less than waiting, so get a written payoff and set it beside any offer.

Here is how the work usually runs:

  1. Phone (770) 387-5111 for the balance and the name on the bill.
  2. If a lender escrows your tax, check with the servicer that this year is paid.
  3. Send the title company the written payoff.
  4. Make sure the closing statement shows who covers which stretch of the year.

Selling for cash, as-is, avoids repair demands and lender delays. Back taxes still come out of your proceeds, which is why an early payoff request pays off. Bring your deed or parcel number and your latest statement when you call or visit, and keep any receipt for your records.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Bartow County?
faqs.a: Due November 15, with statements mailed around September 15. Mobile home bills fall due April 1.

faqs.q: What is the last day to apply for homestead in Bartow County?
faqs.a: April 1, and the exemption covers only your primary residence.

faqs.q: How many days do I get to appeal a Bartow assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the mailing date on the notice. Your written appeal, sent to the Board of Tax Assessors, needs a postmark inside that window.

faqs.q: Will Bartow County send my bill to the lender?
faqs.a: No, the statement goes to the owner as of January 1, so ask your lender whether escrow covers it. A buyer who closed later in the year can call (770) 387-5111 for a duplicate.

faqs.q: Does Bartow County charge a fee to pay by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Debit and credit payments add 2.5 percent, wherever you make them. A mailed check has no such fee.
